prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · REST endpoints (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Endpoint" · longest unbreakable word 261px · one-line width 261px
  col 2: header "Method" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Auth" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "Rate limit" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 85px · one-line width 670px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"An API reference table for scanning REST endpoints and quickly comparing their method, auth requirement, rate limit, and behavior.","reading":"Readers anchor on the endpoint path, then scan the short Method/Auth/Rate limit control fields, and finally read the Description for behavior. Rows must remain identifiable as units even when descriptions wrap.","groups":["Endpoint stands alone as the row identifier.","Method, Auth, and Rate limit form a compact control-metadata block; they are short categorical values read together.","Description is explanatory prose and should receive the remaining width for readable line lengths."],"keep_intact":["Endpoint paths, especially /api/v1/exports/{jobId}/download","HTTP methods such as DELETE","Auth values such as Bearer and Admin","Rate values such as 600/min","Description words and identifiers should not be split mid-token"],"may_wrap":["Description prose across several lines","The 'Rate limit' header between words if necessary","Other short headers only as a last resort"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[282,76,67,78,216],"idea":"Description-first: keep every endpoint path on one line at its exact minimum, compress the control columns, let the Rate limit header wrap, and give all remaining width to prose."},{"name":"B","widths":[300,76,67,89,187],"idea":"Balanced/header-clean: add breathing room to the endpoint column and keep every header on one line, accepting a somewhat narrower description column."},{"name":"C","widths":[282,90,80,95,172],"idea":"Control-first: keep endpoints intact but give Method, Auth, and Rate limit comfortable, clearly separated columns; the description wraps more and rows grow taller."}]}
